grammar.explanation: This pattern describes an impression based on appearance: someone or something looks a certain way.
This pattern means doing one action while doing another. The same person performs both actions.
This pattern expresses a decision to do something.
This pattern expresses attempting an action or being just about to perform it.
This pattern presents another person's action as a favor or something appreciated by the speaker or viewpoint character.
This pattern means that merely doing the stated action is enough to produce the following result.
This pattern indicates that an event appears likely or seems about to happen.

patternSegments.text: Verb ta-form + ことがある / こともある

grammar.explanation: This pattern expresses having had an experience. The additive version emphasizes that the experience has also occurred.
This pattern strongly emphasizes the preceding noun. Here it conveys determination that this year, especially, should be different.
This pattern at the end of a sentence expresses a wish or prayer that something will happen.
This pattern can express completion or an unintended action. Here it describes laughing involuntarily.
This pattern highlights a surprising or emotionally striking situation, often conveying disbelief.

patternSegments.text: なんて + Description + んだろう

grammar.explanation: This pattern forms an emotional exclamation meaning how or what a, emphasizing the degree of a quality.
This pattern says that someone has never had the stated experience, adding it to other experiences they have not had. The past negative form describes experience up to a past point.
This pattern checks a memory or asks for confirmation of something the speaker cannot clearly recall.
This pattern expresses that an action does not happen easily or despite an expectation that it would.
This pattern describes a change into a new habit, behavior, or ability.
This pattern expresses a deliberate decision to do something.
This pattern offers a suggestion, often with the conversational force of asking why someone does not simply take that action.
This pattern presents an action as an arrangement or outcome that has come about, rather than emphasizing a personal decision.
This pattern combines a limiting expression with a negative predicate to mean that only the stated option is available.
This pattern describes another person's apparent desire based on their words or behavior.
This pattern describes attempting an action or being just about to perform it.
This pattern contrasts what is expected to be true with an observed situation that contradicts it.
This pattern expresses previous experience. Its past form here says that Michiko had seen the photograph before.
This pattern connects two actions performed by the same person at the same time, meaning while doing something.
This pattern expresses an attempt or being about to do something. Here Michiko was about to start reading.
This pattern describes a resulting state created by someone's deliberate action. The magazine has been placed on the table and remains there.
This pattern describes the degree of a quality through a result or comparison. Here the heat is enough to cause sweating.
This pattern presents an imagined resemblance, meaning as though or just like. It describes the feeling of having returned home.
This pattern lists representative activities without claiming to list everything. One paired list counts as one occurrence.
This pattern describes a change in ability or habitual behavior. Here it means that Sosuke began doing seasonal work regularly.
This pattern presents an action as something the subject receives from another person. Here Sosuke receives instruction from an elderly neighbor.
This pattern emphasizes an overwhelming feeling or condition, meaning extremely or so much that one cannot help it.
This pattern expresses permission. In a question, it asks whether doing something is allowed.
This pattern expresses a wish that a situation would become possible or come true, meaning I wish or it would be nice if.
This pattern is a casual contraction combining completion with a conditional suggestion. Here it means why don't you just go ahead and do it.
This pattern presents another person's action as welcome or beneficial to the speaker. Here Sosuke imagines how happy Michiko's staying would make him.
This pattern expresses a hope that something will happen or turn out well.
With a negative predicate, this pattern means that something does not happen easily or readily, despite expectations or effort.
After a dictionary-form verb, this pattern expresses inability to perform that action.
This pattern means before an action or change has happened. Here it emphasizes that fewer than five minutes had passed.
After a dictionary-form verb, this pattern states the purpose of an action, meaning in order to.
With a verb stem, this pattern describes an action that is about to happen or nearly happens. Its attributive form can describe a feeling strong enough to bring about an action.
This pattern is a conversational contraction expressing a completed action, often with surprise, regret, or a sense that it happened unintentionally.
This pattern informally expresses necessity. The rest of the obligation expression is often omitted in conversation.
Between actions, this pattern describes a repeated sequence: one action happens, then the other, over and over.
At the end of a statement, this pattern expresses a wish or prayer that the stated situation will come true.
This conversational pattern reports an explanation heard from someone else, meaning apparently or they say.
This pattern singles something out with dismissive or emphatic feeling. Here it dismisses concern about Sachi and strongly rejects the claim that the inn is dirty.
This pattern places a prohibitive ending after a dictionary-form verb to give a direct command not to do something.
This pattern presents an intended or attempted action. Here the following action is performed in an attempt to hand over the ticket.
This pattern follows a past-form verb and indicates that the resulting state continues while another action occurs.
This pattern attaches to a negative verb stem and means without doing the action. Here it describes leaving without speaking.
This pattern is a casual contraction expressing completion, often with regret or concern. Here its past form conveys fear that Michiko has already left.
This pattern takes a proposed topic or condition as its premise. Here it means that if the coffee is Sōsuke's, its quality will be fine.
This pattern expresses being able to receive someone else's action as help or a favor. The person performing the action is marked as its source.
This pattern means every member of a set, regardless of which one is considered. Here it includes the sea at every time of day.
This pattern repeats the same marking to include both groups equally. Here the cafe is popular with travelers and island residents alike.
